blocks.text: Keyword search matches words; vector search matches meaning. An embedding model turns a query ("cheap flights to the beach") and every document into vectors of a few hundred to a few thousand numbers, positioned so that semantically similar things are close together. Search becomes: find the stored vectors nearest to the query vector. This powers semantic search, recommendations ("items like this"), deduplication, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

head: Similarity
Formula
Notes
rows: Equals cosine when vectors are normalised; fastest

blocks.text: Comparing the query with every vector (brute force) is exact but O(n·d): fine for a million vectors on a GPU, too slow for a billion. ANN indexes trade a little recall for orders-of-magnitude speed.

items: **HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World):** a multi-layer proximity graph. Search starts at a sparse top layer, greedily walks toward the query, and drops to denser layers. Excellent recall/latency; memory-hungry (vectors plus graph links in RAM); supports incremental inserts. Tune M (links per node) and efSearch (breadth of search).
**IVF (inverted file):** k-means clusters the vectors; a query searches only the nprobe nearest clusters. Tune nprobe for recall vs speed.
**PQ (product quantisation):** compresses each vector into a few bytes by quantising sub-vectors — 10–50× smaller, enabling billions of vectors per node at some recall cost. Often combined as IVF-PQ.
**DiskANN / SPANN:** graph or cluster indexes designed to keep most data on SSD.
Real queries add constraints: tenant, language, date, permissions.
**Post-filtering** (ANN first, filter after) can return too few results when the filter is selective.
**Pre-filtering / filtered HNSW** applies the filter during traversal; or partition the index per tenant when tenants are large.
Enforce document-level permissions at retrieval time, using ACL metadata stored with each chunk.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Retrieving across all tenants and relying on the LLM prompt to "ignore documents the user can't see". Permissions must be enforced before retrieval results leave the store.

head: Lever
Effect
rows: Too large dilutes meaning; too small loses context
Catches exact terms (IDs, error codes, names) embeddings blur
Big precision gains on the final few results
Measures what the ANN index loses

items: Store the embedding model version with each vector; a model change means re-embedding everything — run old and new indexes side by side and switch.
Shard by tenant or hash; replicate for query throughput; HNSW memory ≈ n × (4·d bytes + ~100–200 bytes of links).
Options range from libraries (FAISS, hnswlib) to extensions (pgvector) to search engines (OpenSearch, Elasticsearch) and dedicated databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, Qdrant).

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: I'd chunk and embed documents, store them in an HNSW index with tenant and ACL metadata, run hybrid retrieval with BM25, fuse and re-rank the top 50 with a cross-encoder, and pass the best 8 chunks to the model.
